title: Knowledge check: Creating Elements Dynamically

questions.prompt: Which principle best guides a correct implementation of creating elements dynamically?
options: Skip error handling and assume the default browser state is always correct.
Load multiple library copies and rely on whichever one executes last.
DOM manipulation changes document content. Use text setters for plain text, create elements with known attributes, and avoid inserting untrusted data as HTML.
Render user-controlled strings as HTML so the browser can infer their meaning.
questions.answer_key: DOM manipulation changes document content. Use text setters for plain text, create elements with known attributes, and avoid inserting untrusted data as HTML.
questions.explanation: DOM manipulation changes document content. Use text setters for plain text, create elements with known attributes, and avoid inserting untrusted data as HTML. Apply this principle with the API/version documentation linked in the lesson.

questions.prompt: Which check is most useful after trying creating elements from html strings?
options: Bind another global handler after every render without cleanup.
Assume the first attempt succeeded and skip verification.
Use a removed jQuery API as the default for new code.
Use creating elements from html strings deliberately, then inspect the actual DOM, request, or event result.
questions.answer_key: Use creating elements from html strings deliberately, then inspect the actual DOM, request, or event result.
questions.explanation: A focused observation checks behavior rather than assuming the method call guarantees the intended result. Include an edge case when the state or inputs can vary.

questions.prompt: Which verification approach best supports professional work with creating elements dynamically?
options: Test a normal path and a relevant edge/failure path, and record expected versus actual behavior.
Test only the first render and publish immediately.
Move answer keys and private configuration into frontend code.
Replace all native browser APIs with jQuery whether needed or not.
questions.answer_key: Test a normal path and a relevant edge/failure path, and record expected versus actual behavior.
questions.explanation: Expected-versus-actual checks, relevant edge cases, and recorded limitations make the implementation easier to debug and review.
